metadata.title: Claude, First Run.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: what actually happens the first time Claude picks up a documented skill? Lands the carry-out that a skill is a folder of plain-language instructions Claude reads before it acts, not a built-in capability.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — redo of a skill-teardown source with no recurring anchor visual; B03's scope box is referenced, not replayed, at BCRY

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude's first-run behavior is just built in — hardwired into the model. It isn't. It's written down, in a skill file Claude reads before it acts. Here's what that file actually contains.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude just runs first-run — it's built in, right?', hesitates on 'built', corrects to 'written', lands 'What's really there?'

props.text:

first-run — it's
built in, right?
What's really there?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('built' -> 'written') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: This particular skill is called first-run. Its SKILL.md file holds the whole instruction set, in plain language — no hidden code, no separate logic buried somewhere else. Whatever Claude does, it's written right there.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder labelled first-run/ opens to one file, SKILL.md, marked as the instruction set

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder, and one file
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'first-run/' on cream. It opens to reveal a single file card, '📄 SKILL.md', which gets a crimson outline and the label 'the instruction set'. A footer line reads 'The file is the program.'

beats.narration_text: The pipeline is in the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it. Linear — no branching unless the step says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Three phases in sequence: Read SKILL.md, Execute each step, Return the result

production_viz.label: Linear execution, start to finish
production_viz.mechanic: YOUR REQUEST enters on the left, flows through three connected phase boxes — 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute each step' (crimson-outlined), 'Return the result' — to RESULT on the right. A single straight arrow path; no branch lines anywhere in frame.

beats.narration_text: first-run's job, spelled out in its own words: check the environment, run one safe browser-only task, then open the trajectory viewer. Claude follows that exact sequence, every time. It has nothing to say about a task the file never described.

shot.new_visual_element: Three specified steps inside a bounded box; a dashed boundary marks what the file never covers

production_viz.label: Exactly this far, and no further
production_viz.mechanic: A solid-outlined box holds three listed steps — 'check environment', 'run one safe browser task', 'open trajectory viewer' — each with a small crimson checkmark as it's read. Outside the box, a dashed boundary line separates it from an empty grey field with a faint '?' — no label, no verdict, just what the file doesn't cover.

beats.narration_text: A skill isn't a built-in capability — it's a folder of plain-language instructions Claude reads before it acts, and follows exactly, only as far as the file goes.

props.quote: A skill isn't a built-in capability — it's a folder of plain-language instructions Claude reads before it acts, and follows exactly, only as far as the file goes.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take any set of detailed instructions — a style guide, a runbook, a SKILL.md if you have one — paste it into Claude, and ask it to walk you through what it will do, step by step, before it does anything. That one clause, 'before you do it,' is what surfaces the real logic underneath. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Here are my detailed instructions: [paste your SKILL.md, runbook, or style guide]. Before you do anything, walk me through exactly what you're going to do, step by step, and why.

beats.narration_text: Claude, First Run. Liam, in for Bear.
